newsitem.title: MEXICO: MORE THAN 20 ARRESTED AS MEXICANS FETE SOCCER WIN.
newsitem.headline: MORE THAN 20 ARRESTED AS MEXICANS FETE SOCCER WIN.

text.p: Police arrested 22 people in Mexico City on Wednesday after hundreds of fans congregated at a central monument to celebrate their soccer team's 3-1 defeat of Honduras, government news agency Notimex said.

The arrests were for "damage to vehicles, passers-by and the Angel of Independence (monument)", Notimex said, adding that one policeman was injured by a flying object during the festivities after the World Cup qualifying match.
Mexican soccer fans frequently mass at the Angel on the central Reforma boulevard to celebrate victories, hurling fireworks and objects at each other and police.
Notimex said about 200 police were on hand to maintain public order. Damage to the monument included graffiti and uprooting of grass, it added.

Earlier on Wednesday, Mexico trounced Honduras with three first-half goals in a victory that virtually assured them of a place in the next qualifying round for the 1998 World Cup, to be held in France.
The match was played in Mexico City's Azteca stadium before an estimated 114,000 fans.
